newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power retains strength ahead of cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power retains strength ahead of cold.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-West remained strong Thursday, supported by forecasts for colder weather this weekend throughout most of the region, industry sources said.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) were steady to slightly higher in the $19.00-22.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) area for Friday delivery, traders said.
Forecasters called for temperatures as low as 18 degrees below-normal through Sunday in the region.
Peak, non-firm prices for next week at ECAR were assessed in the $20.50-21.00 area.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was little changed in the $12.50-14.00 area.
"Outer months are still strong. People are looking ahead to the winter," said one power marketer.
Peak ECAR power prices for December were talked in the $19.45-20.10 range.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power prices for Friday delivery covered a wide range today, but most trading was confirmed done in the $18.00-20.00 area, traders said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power prices edged lower into the $8.50-9.50 area, down from Wednesday's range of $9.00-10.00 per MWh.

In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), next-day, non-firm peak power prices indicated some marginal strength at $19.00-22.00 as the region awaited the arrival of cold temperatures and the possibility of snow.
Off-peak next day MAIN power was stable in the $12.00-14.00 per MWh area.

Commonwealth Edison reported earlier Thursday that its 789 megawatt Quad Cities nuclear unit 1 was boosting power after cutting output over the weekend for repairs. The Illinois unit had been reduced to about half-power.
Peak non-firm next-day power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) were talked stronger in the $22.00 area, as compared to Wednesday's levels at $18.00-20.50, with offers heard as high as $22.50.
Sources attributed the strength to the cold front expected to arrive in the eastern SPP region this weekend.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were reported to be steady to slightly higher in the $13.00-15.00 area, traders said.

Peak December SPP power, however, was talked slightly softer in the $21.80-22.25 range, as compared to Wednesday's discussion at $22.60-22.90. The January SPP market hovered in the $22.70-23.00 area, traders said.
Despite forecasts for significantly colder temperatures this weekend throughout the Midcontinent, the weather is expected to moderate by early next week.
